question: Change the Labels field in metav1.ObjectMeta from map[string]string to a new named type LabelMap requiring accessor methods. ObjectMeta is embedded in every Kubernetes resource type. Which files across ArgoCD, cert-manager, external-secrets, Prometheus, Loki, and OpenTelemetry Operator would break?
summary: Changing metav1.ObjectMeta.Labels from map[string]string to a named struct type LabelMap (with accessor methods) would break any Go file that directly assigns a map literal, initializes with make(map[string]string), uses direct subscript access obj.Labels["key"], iterates with for k, v := range obj.Labels, or passes .Labels as map[string]string to functions. The change is extremely pervasive since ObjectMeta is embedded in every Kubernetes resource.

breaking_patterns.pattern_1: Direct map assignment: obj.Labels = map[string]string{...} — type mismatch, LabelMap is not map[string]string
breaking_patterns.pattern_2: make() initialization: obj.Labels = make(map[string]string) — same type mismatch
breaking_patterns.pattern_3: Map subscript access: obj.Labels["key"] — only valid on map types, not a struct LabelMap
breaking_patterns.pattern_4: Range iteration: for k, v := range obj.Labels — only valid if LabelMap is iterable (i.e., underlying map), but if it is a struct, range fails
breaking_patterns.pattern_5: Type passing: func(labels map[string]string) called with obj.Labels — type mismatch
breaking_patterns.pattern_6: maps.Copy / reflect operations that expect map[string]string
